blocks.task_summary: For the geometric series case: show p = ±1/√3; show convergence; given p > 0 and S∞ = 3+√3, find x.
method_path: Form ratio of consecutive terms r = (p ln x)/(ln x) = p and r² = ((1/3)ln x)/(ln x) = 1/3
Equate to obtain p² = 1/3, hence p = ±1/√3
Note |p| = 1/√3 < 1, therefore the geometric series converges
Apply S∞ = a/(1−r) with a = ln x, r = p = 1/√3 (p > 0)
Set S∞ = 3+√3 and solve for ln x = 2
accepted_alternatives: Set r = p and r² = 1/3 directly without explicit ratio of log terms
Consider powers of x: 1/p = p/(1/3) yielding p² = 1/3
Use r instead of p in the convergence argument

evidence.basis: M1 for attempt to use ratio from consecutive terms; A1 for p² = 1/3 or r = ±1/√3 leading to p = ±1/√3 AG
R1 for |p| = 1/√3 < 1 ⇒ convergence AG; (A1) for S∞ = ln x/(1−1/√3) = 3+√3; A1 for solving to ln x; A1 for x = e²; total [6 marks]

blocks.task_summary: For the arithmetic series case: show p = 2/3; write d = k ln x; given S_n = ln(1/x³), find n.
method_path: Set up common difference: p ln x − ln x = (1/3)ln x − p ln x
Compute d = (2/3)ln x − ln x = −(1/3)ln x
Substitute a = ln x, d = −(1/3)ln x into S_n = (n/2)[2a + (n−1)d]
Equate to −3 ln x, cancel ln x
accepted_alternatives: Use arithmetic mean u₂ = (u₁+u₃)/2 to find p = 2/3
Find d using u₃ = (1/3)ln x then back-substitute to find p
List first 9 terms and observe that first 7 sum to 0, 8th and 9th sum to −3 ln x

evidence.basis: M1 attempt to find difference or arithmetic mean; A1 correct equation; A1 p = 2/3 AG; A1 d = −(1/3)ln x

(M1) substitute into S_n and equate to ln(1/x³); (A1)(A1)(A1) for ln(1/x³)=−3ln x and correct S_n working; A1 equation without ln x; (M1) form quadratic; (M1) solve quadratic; A1 n=9; total [12 marks]
